findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before prescribing `total == 1` for the rate-limit sweep, verify that each of the ten enumerated mutation members makes exactly one underlying client call (or document the per-member expected count), so the tightened assertion doesn't reject correct multi-call implementations.
evidence: test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py:110-145: _RateLimitedClient.__getattr__ returns a function counting under `attempts[name]`; total = sum(attempts.values()) counts all client-method invocations across the member call

The plan prescribes `total == 1` without verifying that each listed member (create_issue, update_issue, add_comment, add_label, remove_label, transition_issue_by_name, set_relationship, delete_issue, delete_issue_link, set_parent) makes exactly one client call in its implementation
Plan text: 'the rate-limit sweep asserts `total == 1` per member' — no qualification for members that may legitimately touch multiple client attributes
findings.finding: The plan's prescribed fix for 2944 item 4 — changing `assert total <= 1` to `assert total == 1` — may incorrectly reject correct transport members that legitimately make more than one client call internally. The existing test's `_RateLimitedClient` uses `__getattr__` to intercept ALL client attribute accesses; `total = sum(attempts.values())` accumulates every distinct client-method invocation across the entire member call. A transport mutation that internally calls two client methods (e.g., fetches a field value before setting it, or calls a lookup then a mutating method) would produce `total == 2` for correct, non-retrying behavior — failing the tightened assertion. The plan neither verifies that all ten enumerated mutation members make exactly one client call nor provides a fallback if any legitimately make two.
findings.location: 2944-dd3f-e982-4359 AC / 'Acceptance criteria': 'the rate-limit sweep asserts `total == 1` per member'
scenarios: A transport member like `transition_issue_by_name` that fetches available transitions first and then calls the transition would produce total==2, failing the new assertion while never retrying
The tightened assertion rejects correct code, forcing an implementer to either weaken the assertion back to <=1 or restructure the transport member — neither of which was the plan's intent
findings.suggested_fix: Audit the ten mutation members' implementations before mandating `total == 1`. For members that legitimately make two client calls (e.g., `transition_issue_by_name` fetching then calling), prescribe `total == <n>` with the expected n documented. Alternatively, assert `no_sleep == []` and `total >= 1` (it reached the client at all) plus the absence of a second attempt after the first 429 — which is the actual invariant.

Re-derivation guidance: 'run `find_referencing_symbols` on each symbol the plan changes to get every structural reference, AND separately grep the codebase for that symbol's name as a string' — both steps are required; the plan only performed the second.
findings.finding: The `bd9e` child ticket's consumer enumeration for `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` was derived exclusively by `git grep` (string search), as stated in the plan's own text. The Re-derivation guidance requires BOTH a structural symbol-reference lookup (find_referencing_symbols / LSP) AND a string grep — one without the other is an incomplete derivation method. The plan explicitly notes the LSP limitation and uses that to justify skipping the structural search, but this is exactly the case the criterion flags: a correct result from an unsound method is luck, not evidence.
findings.location: bd9e-0740-1b47-47f8 § 'Every consumer of the symbol, enumerated': "A repo-wide `git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` (string grep, not just a semantic reference search — the LSP does not see string/attribute access reliably) returns exactly seven sites, and the plan accounts for all of them"
scenarios: Any future structural reference to `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` introduced via dynamic dispatch (e.g., `getattr(module, '_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE')`, `monkeypatch.setattr(..., '_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE', ...)`) would be invisible to string grep and missed by the plan's method — though no such reference currently exists, the derivation method provides no guarantee.

The plan's explicit justification ('the LSP does not see string/attribute access reliably') inverts the correct guidance: LSP catches structural imports and attribute access reliably; string grep catches dynamic string references. Skipping LSP because it misses dynamic references leaves the structural reference graph unverified.
